content: 185.220.101.47 is a known Tor exit node commonly used in credential stuffing and brute force campaigns. Observed in multiple threat intelligence feeds including AbuseIPDB and Shodan. Recommend blocking at perimeter firewall.

DNS tunneling via DGA (Domain Generation Algorithm) is a common C2 technique. Indicators: high query volume, random-looking subdomains, low TTL values. Tools: DNScat2, Cobalt Strike DNS beacon. Detection: monitor queries/minute per host, query entropy score.

Pass-the-Hash (PtH) attack allows adversaries to authenticate using NTLM hashes without knowing plaintext passwords. MITRE ATT&CK: T1550.002. Detection: correlate Logon Type 3 events (network logon) with hash-based auth in Windows Security logs.

Escalation procedure: Tier-1 analysts should escalate to Tier-2 when: (1) critical severity incidents are confirmed, (2) lateral movement is detected, (3) data exfiltration is suspected, (4) executive accounts are involved. Escalation requires incident ID and brief summary.

Credential stuffing attacks typically use leaked credential databases. Indicators: high volume login failures from single IP, multiple account targets, user-agent strings from automation tools (Python-requests, curl). Mitigation: rate limiting, CAPTCHA, MFA enforcement.

Macro-enabled Office documents are a primary delivery mechanism for malware. When WINWORD.EXE spawns cmd.exe or powershell.exe, this is a high-confidence indicator of malicious macro execution. Invoke-Mimikatz is a PowerShell implementation of credential dumping.
